name: Linezolid
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.indication: Nosocomial or community-acquired pneumonia; complicated skin infections
usual_adult_dose.dose: 600 mg IV or oral every 12 hours for 10 to 14 days
600 mg every 12 hours for 14 to 28 days

key_interactions.effect: Linezolid is a reversible MAO inhibitor (label).

key_interactions.drug_or_class: Serotonergic drugs (SSRIs, SNRIs, tricyclics, triptans, meperidine, buspirone)

key_interactions.action: Start vasopressors at lower doses and titrate.

contraindications: Taking an MAO inhibitor or within 2 weeks of one
monitoring: Lactate or bicarbonate if recurrent vomiting

pk.metabolism: Morpholine ring oxidation to two inactive metabolites (A and B)
pk.excretion_renal_pct: About 30% unchanged in urine (plus 40% metabolite B, 10% metabolite A)
